# ENABLE_REMOTE_SYNC

Moved verbatim from `CLAUDE.md` to keep that file lean. Read it only when working on this topic.

- **`ENABLE_REMOTE_SYNC=true/false`**: per-stack flag prompted for by `make new`, wiring up Metabase's "Remote Sync" feature (git-backed collection/library sync, EE-only — settings live in `metabase-enterprise.remote-sync.settings` in the product source, not this repo). Like `ENABLE_METABOT`, it needs no external container — just `compose/remote-sync-overlay.yml` (wired into `scripts/common.sh`'s `compose()` the same way). When true, `start.sh` calls `ensure_remote_sync_repo` then `ensure_remote_sync_checkout` (both in `common.sh`) before `compose up -d metabase`:
  - `ensure_remote_sync_repo` idempotently `git init --bare`s a repo at `data/remote-sync/<COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME>/` (gitignored via the blanket `data/` entry; removed by `nuke.sh` alongside `metabot-debug-logs/`) **and seeds it with one empty commit on `main`**. The seed commit is required, not cosmetic — confirmed live: Metabase's own connection check (`has-data?` in `metabase-enterprise.remote-sync.source.git`, `(< 0 (count (branches source)))`) rejects a zero-branch repo even in read-write mode with "Cannot connect to uninitialized repository," and a plain `git init --bare` alone leaves HEAD as an unborn symref with no real `refs/heads/*`. A bare repo has no working tree to commit into directly, so seeding goes through a throwaway non-bare clone (`git clone` → `commit --allow-empty` → `push` → discard). The function also verifies its own postcondition (a real ref exists) instead of trusting exit codes alone — this repo has a documented history of Windows antivirus intermittently interfering with freshly-written files (see the nyctaxi `curl --retry-all-errors` note), and once genuinely reproduced a silently-empty bind mount this way that only surfaced as a confusing JGit error deep in the Metabase UI.
  - `ensure_remote_sync_checkout` clones a normal (non-bare) working-tree copy of that same repo to `data/remote-sync-checkout/<COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME>/` (also gitignored, also removed by `nuke.sh`) purely so it's browsable — the bare repo has no working tree, so `ls`/Explorer/VSCode show nothing there; open the checkout folder instead (`code data/remote-sync-checkout/<stack>`, or Add Folder to Workspace) and `git pull` inside it by hand to refresh after a push. Only clones once — an existing checkout is never force-refreshed, so it's safe to treat as a normal folder.

  The overlay bind-mounts the bare repo dir read-write into the container at `/remote-sync/repo.git` and sets `MB_REMOTE_SYNC_URL=file:///remote-sync/repo.git` + `MB_REMOTE_SYNC_TYPE=read-write` — both are real Metabase Settings with `:can-read-from-env? true`, so this is a legitimate config path, not a workaround; `file://` URLs are explicitly allowed by the product's own `check-git-settings!`. Deliberately does **not** set `remote-sync-transforms` (no env-var equivalent exists for it at all — `:can-read-from-env?` is absent from that defsetting, admin-API/UI only) or pick which collections/branch sync — those are left for the user to enable by hand in Admin > Remote Sync once the stack is up, since transforms sync is an explicit all-or-nothing toggle that shouldn't be silently flipped on by scaffolding. Needs an EE image (already the default here) and a license token covering at least `transforms-basic` if you also want to test transforms syncing; a bare `remote-sync` feature check exists in code but isn't actually enforced anywhere as of this writing. Minimum Metabase version for transform support specifically: `1.59.1`+. The export/push action itself (`POST /api/ee/remote-sync/export`, body `{"branch": "..."}`) is async and single-flight — a second call while one is running 400s, which the FE surfaces as a generic "Something went wrong" toast rather than a "already in progress" message; not a bug, just don't trigger two exports at once (e.g. one via the UI and one via a script/curl).
